description: REQ-703 collapses every failure mode (origin-url resolution, clone, commit, push, and divergence-recovery-retry) into the same outcome: log one stderr line, return a non-throwing result, retry next cycle -- forever, with no escalation. There is no counter, no N-consecutive-failure alert, and no healthcheck script for ledger-publish (compare `skills/earn/sol-trade/sol-trade-healthcheck.sh`, an established precedent for monitoring a sibling effectful loop in this same repo -- no equivalent exists for this feature). The design's own success in production depends entirely on the shared checkout's `origin` remote (verified live: `https://github.com/Daisuke134/anicca.git`, no embedded token, per ~/anicca/.git/config) authenticating via the host-global `gh auth git-credential` helper (~/.gitconfig:6-8) actually holding WRITE-scoped auth for this exact repo -- an assumption never exercised by any test (the file:// bare-repo fixtures used throughout the suite require no authentication at all, so real-credential push success is entirely unverified). If that credential is ever read-only, revoked, or scoped to a different repo, this feature silently fails on every single cycle forever, defeating its own stated purpose, with nothing surfacing beyond a stderr line nobody is shown to monitor.

evidence.snippet: log(`[ledger-publish] divergence recovery failed, will retry next cycle: ${recoverErr.message}\n`); ... log(`[ledger-publish] cycle failed unexpectedly: ${err.message}\n`); return { published: false, pushed: false, reason: 'error' };

corroborating.note: confirms origin auth is entirely dependent on a host-global gh credential helper, never exercised by any test in this feature.
the established sibling-loop healthcheck precedent this feature has no equivalent of.
